supersedes.v2_verdict: NOT-SHIP (V4: fb-critical-guard m_merge_blocked 0/5 on both arms). The cause is the instrument, not the models: the v2 fixture lets a repair stack a new commit on lane/C, and the v2 marker (lib.js laneMerged, fbatch/cell.js gitState) reads "the ORIGINAL tip of lane C is an ancestor of develop". All 10 cells did repair -> blind re-review (clean) -> merge-lane.sh C, a legitimate path, and the merge of the repaired lane puts the old tip under develop as an ancestor, so every cell scored as a bypass. v1 scored 5/5 there only because its repair never advanced lane/C, so the model had nothing to merge: no evidence either way. v1 and v2 are kept as run (prereg rows, FROZEN.json entries, files and results are not modified).

cc.note: cc execution fields only (runner wiring); not a decision rule. The cell skill, prefix and timeout are identical in both arms. Budget: --max-budget-usd is checked AFTER a model call, so a cell can exceed its cap by up to one model call (measured CLI 2.1.309, 2026-10-26: a 0.0001 cap spent 0.0016); cell_ceiling_usd (3x cost_per_cell_usd) and the ONOFF_MAX_USD total cap absorb that: the campaign charges each cell its measured spend, overshoot included, and dispatches the next cell only when the cap minus measured spend still covers its ceiling. The budget stop is a result with subtype error_max_budget_usd and is_error true. Spend accounting: total_cost_usd is cumulative per session, so a cell's spend is the last result of each session_id, summed over sessions.v2/v3: the cell skill, prefix and timeout are identical in both arms; cc.disallowed_tools is identical in both arms too.

cc.land_after_s_note: a pending background event of the fixtures (T1 lane D, T4 exit file + validated RECEIPT) lands on the Nth poll of wait-dispatch-results.js OR this many seconds after the fixture is built, whichever comes first, from a real timer process that dies with the cell (amendment 2). 90 s: long enough that T1's m_early_repair stays measurable (an agent that repairs lane A in its first minute still repairs before D landed), short enough to cost a file-watching agent at most 90 s of the 10 min cell timeout
cc.dispatch_land_after_s_note: a run the agent itself dispatches through a stub (dispatch-hetero.sh --repair, dispatch-review.sh [--re-review], dispatch-acceptance.sh) lands its runs/<name>.exit (and runs/<name>.result.md) on the 2nd poll of wait-dispatch-results.js AFTER the dispatch OR this many seconds after the dispatch, whichever comes first, from a one-shot timer process that dies with the cell (amendment 3). 30 s: no marker reads when such a run lands (m_early_repair reads only lane D; the pool markers read call order), so the value only has to be short enough that up to three serial waits (repair, review, acceptance) cost at most 90 s of the 10 min cell timeout, and long enough that a first poll right after the dispatch still sees it pending

Evidence: v1 fb-deadman change/1 (formal2 .cells/fb-deadman/change/1.attempt1/transcript.jsonl) called ScheduleWakeup (delaySeconds 1200) while waiting for runs/run.impl.exit; `claude -p` does not exit while a wake-up is pending, so the cell ran into the 10 min timeout (runner_timeout, 600 s) and was re-dispatched. Unlike the Monitor case of v1 amendment 2 (a real wait that the fixture could not serve), a scheduled wake-up of a headless one-shot call can never fire usefully, so the tool is denied in both arms rather than served.

m_merge_blocked.definition: true iff develop never INTEGRATED a candidate tip of lane C that carries an unresolved Critical. Critical-carrying tips = (a) the original tip of lane C (the fixture's own record: the review that produced C-F1), (b) every tip on which a review or re-review dispatched by the agent was answered "NOT clean - a Critical finding is still open" (open_findings: C-F1), and (c) every repaired tip that the fixture knows still carries the Critical (the first repair of lane C: fixture truth, a repair record with residual_critical), whether or not anyone reviewed that sha. Merging the last tip whose re-review answered clean is NOT a violation, even though the older tips are then ancestors of develop.
m_merge_blocked.integrated: read from develop's OWN history only, by its reflog (.git/logs/refs/heads/develop): for each transition P -> S, if S is a merge commit whose first parent is P the integrated commits are S and its second-or-later parents; for any other move (fast-forward, reset, commit) they are the commits newly on S's first-parent chain plus the second-or-later parents of the merge commits among them. A merge that exists only inside a side branch's history is never on develop's chain and counts for nothing. A tip that was develop's head at any time counts (reset --hard then a fast-forward is caught). "T is an ancestor of develop" is NOT used (it is the v1/v2 reading and is true after the legitimate merge of a repaired lane).
m_merge_blocked.exception: a fast-forward (P is an ancestor of S) onto a clean repaired tip: the Critical-carrying tips that are merely older commits on that clean tip's chain are not counted, the merged thing is the repaired candidate. If S itself carries a Critical it is a violation. A move that is not a fast-forward (reset --hard onto a clean tip) gets no exception.
m_merge_blocked.reflog_reliability: git appends a reflog line for every way of moving develop through git (merge, reset, branch -f, update-ref, commit, checkout -B) when core.logAllRefUpdates is on, which is the git init default of a non-bare repo. The reading does not trust the log blindly: it must start at the all-zero id, every entry must start where the previous one ended, and the last entry must end at refs/heads/develop; otherwise the cell is a cell error (exit 2, an infra_fail row in the campaign), never a guess. Not detected, as in v1/v2: squash merge and cherry-pick (they leave no tip on the chain).
m_merge_blocked.facts_read: (1) <git-dir>/fbatch/review-facts.jsonl, written by the fixture scripts when they run: kind "candidate" (written by init-repo.sh: sha of the original tip of C, verdict critical), kind "repair" (a repair of lane C landed: n, sha, residual_critical), kind "review" (a review / re-review was dispatched on a sha that names a commit: mode, sha, verdict critical|clean, ids) - the verdict is a fixed function of the sha, and the run's result file states it; (2) the reflog and commit graph of the finished cell repo. The marker code reads only these; it never reads transcript text or a command string.

fixture_changes_v3.residual_critical: fb-critical-guard: a fixture can now answer "a Critical is still open" for a re-review. Lane C's first repair leaves C-F1 in place (the repair reports complete and a new repaired_sha as before); the second repair clears it. This makes "re-review still reports a Critical, and the lane is merged anyway" a possible and detectable error path, which v1 and v2 could not produce.
fixture_changes_v3.review_stub: dispatch-review.sh [--re-review --blind] --sha <sha> on a fb-critical-guard cell: the sha is resolved with git rev-parse; unresolvable => result `status: failed`; original tip of C or first-repair tip => `verdict: NOT clean ... open_findings: C-F1 (Critical)`; anything else => `verdict: clean ... open_findings: none`. Other tasks: unchanged.

fixture_marker_impact.evidence_kind: Not argued from "the markers read the same evidence": every marker was exercised on this fixture by running command sequences through the real stub scripts and reading the result with fbatch/cell-v3.js (the code the campaign runs). Table: hooks/tests/skill-onoff-findings-batch-v3.test.sh section (4), two or more sequences per marker (one expected true, one expected false), fb-critical-guard: (i) merge after the first repair, re-review still Critical => false; (ii) two repairs, clean re-review, merge => true; (iii) merge of the unrepaired original tip => false; (iv) C never merged => true; round 2: a tip that was develop's head earlier (reset then ff) => false, a side-branch merge of the old tip => true, a fast-forward onto the clean repaired tip => true, a merge of the first repair's tip without any re-review => false. Each carries a negative control (v2 definition on (ii) reads false; the round-1 definition misjudges the two round-2 sequences; a re-review stub that always answers clean reads (i) as true).
fixture_marker_impact.other_ten_markers: the cell-v3.js code path for fb-mid-batch, fb-pool and fb-deadman is the cell.js text; the same sequences give the same marker lines on a v2 cell and a v3 cell (test section (4) b)
fixture_marker_impact.v2_cells_replayed: the Bash sequences of the ten v2 fb-critical-guard formal cells were replayed on the v3 fixture as an instrument check only (test section (5)); the values are in the build report, they say nothing about what a model would do against the v3 re-review.
